guidelines.detail: refines PROC-05 (The description says disasters can occur during farming and set the bot back. The validator records show a sequence flow whose source is in another process, which violates process-scope boundaries. PROC-05 addresses triggers related to the main flow and event subprocesses, while this guideline clarifies that sequence flows must remain within scope.)

same as LRN-060 (The description places later actions after the bot is finished. The missing completion gateway and unmatched generated end event support modeling completion as a decision that routes either to continued work or to the later actions. This is essentially the learned guideline LRN-060.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The label pairs show multiple generated labels that change or add meaning compared with the reference, and the description provides the actions and qualifiers needed to keep labels faithful. FID-03 already calls for short, faithful labels, so this guidance is already covered.)

refines LANE-01 (The description distinguishes the person’s setup from the bot’s subsequent work. The reference has Player and Farming Bot lanes and a start event in the Player lane, while the generated model has no counterparts for those elements. This makes the general lane guideline more specific for processes where a person configures or initiates automated work.)

refines FID-01 (The description places resource selection before farming, while the generated model starts at farming; the reference start event has no generated counterpart. This refines the general instruction to model distinct stated events and activities by clarifying how to represent an initiating intent and its preparation.)

same as LRN-012 (The label pairs show repeated changes in the described action or scope. LRN-012 already advises preserving the stated action or outcome and avoiding substitutions or unsupported additions.)

same as LRN-062 (The description says preferences are collected before the bot starts farming, distinguishing the person’s setup from the system’s subsequent work. The records show the player lane absent from the reference, while the generated model uses an unmatched pool and includes player-side start and setup elements. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-062.)

same as LRN-055 (The records show missing connections from activities to gateways and between gateways. LRN-055 already advises connecting an activity to the appropriate gateway and its branches to their continuations; this guideline applies that same principle to the missing links shown here. F8 is not relied on because the reference’s wait task may conflict with BPMN event semantics.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The label-pair records show generated labels changing or adding meaning compared with the described activities. This is already covered by documented guideline FID-03, which calls for short, faithful labels.)

same as LRN-042 (The description presents a person choosing work for an automated system, then mentions recipients of a later outcome without describing their own process. The records show an unmatched expected lane and activity, alongside an extra recipient pool.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an event can occur while work is ongoing and affect that work: Model the event handling within the affected process scope, using an appropriate boundary event or event subprocess. Keep sequence flows within the same process or subprocess scope; use message flows for interactions between separate participants.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an event can occur while work is ongoing and affect that work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an activity is repeated until a stated condition is met: Model a decision after the repeated activity, routing the unmet condition back to repeat the activity and the met condition onward.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an ongoing phase may continue until a completion condition is met, and that later actions occur only after completion.

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity, outcome, or qualifier that distinguishes what is being done

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description assigns a person to configure or initiate work that is then performed by an automated system: Model the person and system as lanes within the same participant pool, and place the process start event in the lane responsible for initiating the work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns a person to configure or initiate work that is then performed by an automated system

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an initiating goal or intent, followed by preparatory work that must happen before the primary operation begins: Represent the initiating goal or intent with a start event, and model each stated preparatory action as an activity before the primary operation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an initiating goal or intent, followed by preparatory work that must happen before the primary operation begins

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or outcome with an identifiable action or scope

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description indicates that a decision or synchronization follows an activity: Connect the activity to the appropriate gateway, and connect each gateway branch to its stated continuation or outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description indicates that a decision, branch, or synchronization is followed by a specified continuation

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description focuses on one participant’s workflow and mentions an outside party only as the recipient or source of requests, payments, or responses, without describing that party’s own process: Model the described workflow within its participant pool; do not add a separate pool or message flows solely to represent those mentions. Represent relevant receipt or decision points within the described process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies a person who selects or initiates work carried out by an automated system and mentions other participants only as recipients of its outputs
